info.title: 1440 Cloud
info.description:
The 1440 Cloud API lets your systems read and send Apple Messages for Business (AMB) conversations for your organization.

**Authentication**

1. In the 1440 Cloud console, open **Admin → Integrations**, create an integration, and mint an API key. Copy the key; it is shown once.
2. Exchange the key for an access token with `POST /api/v0/auth/integration/token`, sending `Authorization: Bearer <API key>`.
3. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other request.

Access tokens are short-lived; `expiresAt` says when the token expires. Cache the token and reuse it for all requests until shortly before `expiresAt`, then exchange the key again. Do not exchange the key for a new token on every request.

Each endpoint lists the permissions it requires. All listed permissions are required. Endpoints that show **Required Access Level:** Admin also need an integration whose access level is Admin.

**Rate limits**

Requests are rate limited. A `429` response includes `Retry-After`; wait that many seconds before retrying.

**Message content**

`POST /api/v0/messaging/send-raw` takes channel-native content, nested under `data`. Conversation history and webhooks return sent and customer messages as flat fields. Content you read cannot be sent back as-is.

**Webhooks**

Set your webhook URL on the integration in the console. Deliveries are signed using the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) scheme:

- The signing secret is shown once when the integration is created, as `whsec_<base64>`. The signing key is the Base64-decoded value after `whsec_`.
- Compute HMAC-SHA256 of `{Webhook-Id}.{Webhook-Timestamp}.{raw request body}`, Base64-encode it, and compare it with the value after `v1,` in `Webhook-Signature`.
- Reject deliveries whose `Webhook-Timestamp` is more than 5 minutes old.

Delivery turns off if your endpoint responds with `410` or keeps failing; turn it back on with **Outbound webhook delivery enabled** on the integration. You can resend a past delivery with **Replay delivery** in the integration's delivery log.

post.description:
Send text, uploaded media, a published template, or an authentication message to a conversation. Text needs a nonblank `body`, 1–10 uploaded `mediaAssetId` values in `attachmentIds`, or both; for attachments only, set `body` to `""`. Resulting attachments have distinct IDs in `messages[].attachments[].id` for access-URL requests. Template variables must match the template’s declarations.

Request bodies are limited to 5,000,000 bytes. After a timeout, delivery may already have occurred. Reuse `requestMessageId` with identical bytes to replay a successful result, including after opt-out; different bytes return 409. Concurrent requests and retries after an uncertain send can deliver multiple copies, even for conflicting requests. Retry uncertain sends with the same ID and bytes.

**Required Permissions:** `SendMessages`

post.description:
Receive a customer message and conversation details. `message.content` has the same fields as conversation history content. A form response with `private: true` is sensitive. Without `ViewSensitiveResponses`, sensitive content is null and `redacted` is true; attachment metadata and URLs remain available. `eventId` and `Webhook-Id` equal `message.id` and remain stable across retries and replay; `message.createdAt` retains the original timestamp. Unknown routing values are null; an empty `capabilityList` means none reported.

Events are POSTed to the configured webhook URL. Return any 2xx to acknowledge; network errors and non-2xx responses retry with exponential backoff. Deduplicate using `Webhook-Id`.

parameters.description: Event id; retries reuse it.

parameters.description: Delivery signing time in Unix seconds, not event time.

parameters.description: Signature: `v1,<base64(HMAC-SHA256)>` over `Webhook-Id.Webhook-Timestamp.rawBody`.

2XX.description: Acknowledged. Return any 2xx to stop retries.
